answer.rationale:
memory_c2 is the only inherited record that would justify the aggressive move (switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor), and it is the memory whose original context matters most: consolidated summaries of cost wins routinely omit qualification lead time, first-article/PPAP effort, ramp yield, and whether the vendor was ever the *sole* primary at full committed volume. If the archived record shows the switch was a partial or secondary allocation, or occurred with line buffer available, the memory does not transfer to today's situation. That is why it, and not the incumbent-favorable memories, gets the single verification pull.

Current intent is negotiate_terms. The binding constraint is not price discovery, it is the conjunction of a 14-day cliff with no auto-renew, 94% line utilization with zero buffer, and one decision of capacity. Migrating primary supply under those conditions puts delivery risk squarely on the line even if the quoted unit price alone satisfies the 18% mandate, and the stated objective forbids trading delivery risk for TCO. memory_c4 (benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and terms) and memory_c6 (multi-year commitment unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope) both point at the same instrument, and the low-cost quote is live leverage that makes the benchmark credible rather than rhetorical. memory_c1 supports the continuity value of not migrating.

Uncertainty I am deliberately not collapsing: negotiation plus a term commitment may not close the full 18% gap. I am treating the mandate as a target to be approached this cycle, not a guarantee. If the negotiated outcome lands materially short, the honest read is that the remaining gap must be closed by a qualified second source or a staged switch in the next review window, not by an unqualified cutover now. Downstream risk flagged on two counts: (1) a multi-year commitment taken to reach the price target reduces future optionality precisely when a cheaper vendor is emerging, so any term extension should be structured with benchmark/exit provisions rather than pure duration; (2) the low-cost vendor's cost advantage remains unvalidated at full primary volume, so quoting it as a settled fact into the next cycle would propagate an untested figure. Concrete next step regardless of the archive result: open low-cost vendor qualification on a small non-critical allocation so the next review has real data instead of an inherited claim.
